items.title: The Building Blocks of Positioning
items.content_snippet: What does good positioning actually look like? April Dunford, positioning expert and author of Obviously Awesome, breaks it into components: • Competitive alternatives: if you didn't exist, what would a customer do? • Differentiated capabilities: what do you have that the alternatives don't? • Differentiated value: why do those features matter to a business? • The customers who care a lot about that value. items.title: Why Cloudflare Became a Neolab — Michelle Chen, Cloudflare
items.content_snippet: Cloudflare bet early that AI models would get smaller and network latency would matter. Instead models grew to trillions of parameters, so Cloudflare pivoted to serving them. Then System 1 decision models arrived, and Cloudflare trained its own over a weekend and shipped four models in three weeks. Michelle Chen, group PM for Workers AI, tells that story and demos Clef and Cleric alongside an LLM on a CI triage task: about 2x faster, 72% cheaper and 94% fewer tokens, with the same answer. items.title: Execution Is Free. How Ambitious Are You? — Jason Liu, OpenAI
items.content_snippet: When execution is nearly free, ambition is about how you approach the work, not how many tokens you spend. Jason Liu of OpenAI's developer experience team takes on three fears: that AI means more slop, that it erodes critical thinking, and that it will replace us. His answers: own the work you ship, build the language to describe what good looks like, and use AI to pursue the fields you set aside for software.
